data.description:
Three defects found walking the competition walkthrough live.

1. CRITICAL — public CFP confirmation link dead-ends. /f/cfp confirmation offers 'Open your speaker portal'; the magic link authenticates the new submitter, then GET /api/v1/me/portal 404s 'conference not found' because speakerEvent() requires a memberships row with role='speaker'. A public submitter holds a participations row with role='submitter' and no membership. Fix is SPEC.md:625's ruled answer — one honest empty state for a submitter, NOT a speaker membership grant.

2. /api/openapi.json info.description claims 'Mutations carry strong ETag/If-Match optimistic concurrency.' Only 2 of 203 routes declare concurrency if-match (agenda item update and remove). Narrow the sentence to what is true.

3. /f/cfp advertises a CFP close of Apr 30 2027 for an Oct 12-14 2026 conference. NOT a seed artifact: scripts/seed/event.ts has only ever held CFP_CLOSES = 2026-09-13T03:59:59Z (Sep 12 end-of-day ET). The live D1 row was mutated after the last seed. Fix is live data, not code.
data.title: Judge walkthrough: submitter portal dead-ends, OpenAPI overclaims ETag, CFP close date implausible

data.body:
Live data fix shipped for defect 3 — the CFP close date.

Finding: NOT a seed artifact. scripts/seed/event.ts has only ever held CFP_CLOSES = Date.UTC(2026, 8, 13, 3, 59, 59) (Sep 12 end-of-day ET); git log -S confirms no other value in its history, and a fresh local seed reproduces it. The live D1 row had been edited through the product: forms.updated_at was 2026-08-12T20:40:36Z, about an hour before this ticket opened, and the same edit added three form fields the seed does not write (key_takeaway, audience_level, workshop_prerequisites).

Action: UPDATE forms SET closes_at = 1789271999000 WHERE id = 'frm_cfp' AND closes_at = 1809118800000 — one row changed. Prior value 1809118800000 (2027-04-30T21:00Z) is recorded here for reversal. Live /f/cfp now renders 'Closes 9/13/2026' and the form state is still open.

Deliberately NOT touched: the three added form fields. Unattributed live fleet work, out of scope for this ticket, and possibly deliberate demo content.

Noted, not fixed: the /f/cfp header formats closes_at in UTC, so a timestamp meaning 'Sep 12 end-of-day ET' displays as 9/13/2026. Pre-existing, cosmetic, plausible either way — not worth a seed-semantics change on deadline day.

PR #136 merged to main as b95fa130 at 2026-08-12T22:23Z. Reviewed and merged by Eval Fix Orchestrator (ws:6 surface:75), who independently attacked the participation scoping before merging: ?eventId= confirmed a narrowing AND with correct bind ordering; raw s.status confirmed identical to the speaker portal's pre-existing behaviour, not introduced here; getPortal confirmed still behind requireUnscopedSpeakerSession so a cospeaker_profile-scoped session cannot reach the submitter path.

One merge-time detail worth recording: main's 32f9a696 (MRQ-146) had independently narrowed the SAME ETag overclaim in one clause. The conflict was resolved toward this PR's fuller paragraph, and MRQ-146's honesty contract was re-pointed at the new wording in 75c16676 without weakening it — agenda-only scope now asserted by two literals instead of one, the If-Match-appears-once and two-operation assertions untouched.

Defects 1 and 2 are code-only and reach judges only via a deploy; Eval Fix Orchestrator owns that. Defect 3 is already live (see prior comment). Reported to Submission Prep (ws:5 surface:26).

Remaining on this ticket: live click-through verification of the confirmation link against https://marquee.stage11.dev once the deploy lands.

data.body:
Verified state from the defect-fix agent (NOT this ticket's owner — PortalDeadEnd-1 is).

PR #136 merged as b95fa130 and is now DEPLOYED: curl https://marquee.stage11.dev/health -> build acc19c8a52c2, built 2026-08-12T23:01:50Z. acc19c8a is downstream of b95fa130, so the submitter-portal fix is live on the judge-facing site. Defect 3 (CFP close date) was fixed as live data at 21:57Z per this ticket's earlier comment. Defect 2 (OpenAPI If-Match) shipped in the same PR.

All three defects here now appear resolved AND deployed, so this likely belongs at done rather than review. Leaving status and assignment alone: those are the owner's call, not mine.

Ownership note for anyone reading this as orphaned: I walked the same judge loop independently and filed overlapping work, then dropped it once I found #136. My portal fix reached the portal via a participation fallback; #136 follows SPEC.md Amendment 15's ruling (one honest empty state for a submitter, not a speaker-portal grant) and is the correct answer. The only thing I shipped is unrelated to this ticket: PR #139, the speakers-embed surname sort (EMB-04/EMB-12), merged as acc19c8a and live in the same deploy.

**Post-merge review of PR #136 (merged as b95fa130) — 8 findings. Verdict at review time was REQUEST CHANGES; the PR merged before this landed, so these are now defects on `main`.**

Adversarial read by a non-author agent, against the diff `5441cf1c..1c398538`, SPEC §10 (Amendment 15), and PHILOSOPHY. Full `npm test` was green (vitest projects + 187 node tests, ~232s against the 45s objective under fleet contention). One isolated vitest run appeared to fail `meta.test.ts` on MRQ-146's old assertion string; a clean re-run passed 7/7 — stale transform cache, not a real failure.

---

## Security: clean. Do not re-litigate without contrary evidence.

The new submitter path resolves an event and lists submissions without a memberships check. I could not construct a leak.

- **Co-speaker sessions cannot reach the new path.** `getPortal` calls `requireUnscopedSpeakerSession` (`src/routes/portal.routes.ts:1377` → `:267-271`), which 403s any `cospeaker_profile:` roleHint before `portalSnapshot` runs.
- **Cross-person: no.** `submitterSnapshot`'s `EXISTS (… p.person_id = ?)` (`:1006-1012`) and the correlated `participation_role` subquery both bind `auth.personId`.
- **Cross-org: no.** `findSubmitterEvent` filters `e.org_id = auth.orgId` (`:340`); `auth.orgId` is `person.org_id` (`src/lib/auth/auth-middleware.ts:89`); the public form upserts people under the *event's* org (`src/routes/public-form.routes.ts:271`), so a participation cannot straddle orgs in the first place.
- **Speaker path unchanged.** `speakerEvent` is a pure extract-and-rethrow over identical SQL (`:307-315`); every other caller still uses it. `AWAITING_DECISION` is a literal extraction of the same three statuses.
- **No speaker-only data on the submitter payload**: tasks `[]`, handbook `""`, venue count 0, person narrowed to id/name/email.

---

## Findings

**1. A saved draft is told it is under review, and is never offered the one action it needs.** `src/ui/portal/PortalPage.tsx:838,845,846`. Drafts are reachable in this seat: `createDraft`/`autosaveDraft` both write participation rows (`src/routes/public-form.routes.ts:542,587`), and the `draft_resume` magic link mints a normal `roleHint: "login"` session (`src/routes/auth.routes.ts:264,270-283`), so `/portal` opens on a draft. `submitterHeadline` gets it right — "Your draft is saved, not yet submitted" (`:777`) — then everything below contradicts it: `:838` "Nothing is waiting on you" (the draft is waiting entirely on them); `:845` "Yours is in the queue — there is no further step for you here" (it isn't, and there is exactly one); `:846` promises a decision date, and `AWAITING_DECISION` includes `"draft"` (`portal.routes.ts:75,1014`) so the server *invents* the next wave's date for an unsubmitted abstract. The resume URL is never offered — `form_slug` links to `/f/{slug}`, which starts a fresh abstract. Also hits the common mixed case: one submitted + one draft, ordered `updated_at DESC`, so the draft leads the hero. This is the empty-state failure PHILOSOPHY names.

**2. Wave name and decision date are picked by two independent scans.** `PortalPage.tsx:810-814`. `decisionOn` and `waveName` each `.find()` over all submissions separately, so two pending abstracts in different waves print Wave 1's name against Wave 2's date. `per_submitter_limit` makes multiple abstracts real. Read both off one submission, or stop naming a wave you didn't take the date from.

**3. Terminal statuses still get the "a decision is coming" paragraph.** `PortalPage.tsx:812-814,846`. Nothing branches on status below the hero. For rejected, `updateSubmissionStatus` clears `wave_id` (`src/jobs/cascade/decisions.ts:721`, `preserveWave` is accept-only) and `rejected` isn't in `AWAITING_DECISION`, so the reader gets "Your abstract was not selected" followed by "The program team has not set a decision date for this round yet" and step 2's "We write to you either way." Same for `withdrawn`.

**4. A waitlist decision is announced here that the product deliberately does not email.** `portal.routes.ts:1039` returns raw `s.status`; the UI renders "Your abstract is waitlisted" (`PortalPage.tsx:779`). `writeSubmissionDecision` explicitly skips mail for `waitlisted` (`src/jobs/cascade/decisions.ts:1026-1028`), while accept and reject enqueue in the same call — so those two are fine and this one isn't. Before this PR that person had no portal at all (no memberships row → 404), so this is a new disclosure channel for a decision the organizer has not sent. Own data, not a tenancy leak, but it is an organizer-timing decision being made by the portal. **Open: I could not find a spec line saying whether silent-waitlist is intended.** Either confirm it's intended or mask the status until a wave is sent.

**5. `src/api/openapi.ts:99` — "Every other mutation is last-write-wins" is false, and it is a claim this PR introduces.** Two counterexamples in the same document: `POST /api/v1/events/{eventId}/agenda/publish` (`src/routes/agenda.routes.ts:206`) guards on `item.updated_at = ?` plus a count check and throws `409 "the selected Sessions changed while publishing"` (`:273,296-297,301-303`); and `POST` decisions (`src/routes/submission-decisions.routes.ts:87` → `decisions.ts:1011-1024`) writes conditionally on `status <> ?` and fails with "submission changed during decision; retry the confirmed action". A technical judge can falsify this in one request, which is the bar MRQ-146 set. **Every other clause verified true**: `if-match` is on exactly the two agenda-item routes (`agenda.routes.ts:440,511`), agenda item reads carry a strong etag (`agenda.queries.ts:195`, `agenda.routes.ts:335`), `requireIfMatch` demands the exact strong tag (`src/api/concurrency.ts:36-53`), and a stale tag is 409 with the current tag in the `ETag` header (`concurrency.ts:126-129`). Narrowing to "no other mutation uses `If-Match`" would be true. Sweep for further counterexamples before rewording — the claim is universal.

**6. The PR's stated premise is stale, and the repo is public.** At this branch's base (`5441cf1c`, = `main` at the time) the description already read *"Strong `ETag`/`If-Match` optimistic concurrency currently applies only to the two agenda item mutation operations that require it"* — MRQ-146 fixed the overclaim. The new test's docstring (`tests/integration/api/meta.test.ts:127-129`) says the document "used to state that mutations carry `ETag`/`If-Match` optimistic concurrency," which is not what it stated at that base. The commit message carries the same wrong backstory. Fix the comment; the commit message is already in history.

**7. The submitter seat picks the earliest event and cannot reach a second.** `portal.routes.ts:341` orders `e.starts_on ASC`, and the UI fetches `/api/v1/me/portal` with no `eventId` (`PortalPage.tsx:891`) though the route accepts one. Someone with a participation on a past event's submission plus a fresh CFP submission lands on the past event with no navigation to the new one — the same dead end this ticket exists to close, one event over. Inherited from the speaker path, but "earliest" is systematically the wrong choice for a submitter. Check against MRQ-129's multi-event work; at minimum the confirmation link could carry the event.

**8. The zero-submission branch is unreachable, and its neighbours would lie if it weren't.** `PortalPage.tsx:869` vs `findSubmitterEvent` — the event resolves only through a participation on a submission, and `submitterSnapshot`'s `EXISTS` uses the identical predicate, so `submissions.length === 0` cannot occur. `tests/unit/submitter-portal.MRQ-150.test.ts` asserts it anyway; if it ever did occur the hero would still say "Your abstract is in" (`:832`, default `"submitted"`) and step 1 would still say "Yours is in the queue". Either drop the branch or branch the copy with it.

---

## Open question I could not close

`acceptedSpeakerMembershipStatements` filters `role IN ('speaker','co_speaker')` (`src/lib/speaker-membership.ts:87`), so a participant whose only role is `submitter` — reachable via the organizer's participant editor, whose enum includes it (`src/routes/submission-record.routes.ts:40`) — never gets a membership at acceptance, making `PortalPage.tsx:847` ("This page becomes your speaker portal") false for them. The CFP path itself is safe: the public form always writes both a `submitter` and a `speaker` participation (`public-form.routes.ts:279-289`).

## Not verified

Nothing here was exercised against the deployed site — this is source reading plus the local suite.

## Suggested grouping for ticketing

Findings 1–3 and 8 are one ticket (submitter-seat copy and state honesty; medium, delegate). Finding 4 is a product decision before it is a fix. Findings 5–6 are one small ticket (OpenAPI sentence + the stale docstring; low, inline). Finding 7 is its own (event scoping; medium). An independent validation pass is running at c11 `workspace:6 / surface:67` ("PR136 review audit") and should be read before minting.
